query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In single‐phase FCC high-entropy alloys derived from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, the extent of local lattice distortion arising from compositional fluctuations is the primary mechanistic determinant of differences in mechanical properties. Specifically, higher compositional complexity (quinary alloys) increases local strain fields that impede dislocation motion (e.g., through solute-dislocation interactions and inducing more wavy or heterogeneous slip paths) resulting in higher strength (and potentially lower ductility) compared to their quaternary or ternary subsets.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC alloys obtained after standardized thermomechanical processing using equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni (quinary) and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of the constituent count by fabricating alloys that are equiatomic in quinary, quaternary, and ternary compositions under identical processing conditions.
generation.conditions: Room temperature (with potential extension to elevated temperatures) under well-controlled strain rate mechanical testing, complemented by high-resolution microstructural observations (e.g., TEM and high-resolution XRD to assess microstrain).
generation.structural_mediator: The magnitude and spatial distribution of local lattice distortions (microstrain fields) induced by compositional complexity.
generation.mechanism: Increasing the number of elements in the alloy enhances compositional heterogeneity, which increases local lattice distortions. These distortions alter the dislocation behavior by either impeding dislocation glide or modifying the slip mode (e.g., inducing more curved or heterogeneous dislocation paths). In effect, the dislocation–solute interactions modulate yield strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys should show lower levels of local lattice distortion. This reduced distortion would correlate with lower yield strength and a different dislocation slip morphology (e.g., more planar slips) compared to the quinary alloy, which should exhibit higher yield strength along with modified ductility due to the impeded dislocation motion.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni single-phase FCC alloy.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for alloys that are single-phase FCC and processed via similar thermomechanical routes. It may not extend to non-equiatomic compositions, multiphase materials, or alloys with substantially different processing histories.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative relationship between the extent of lattice distortion and the magnitude of the mechanical property changes remains uncertain. In addition, subtle processing-induced residual stresses or microstructural features not related to compositional complexity may complicate the interpretation.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate single-phase FCC alloys for equiatomic quinary, quaternary, and ternary compositions under identical thermomechanical processing conditions. Use high-resolution XRD and TEM to quantitatively map local lattice distortions (microstrain) in each alloy. Conduct standard mechanical tests (e.g., uniaxial tensile or compressive tests) at room temperature to measure yield strength, ductility, and study dislocation behavior through in situ observations.
measurements: Local lattice distortion (measured by microstrain via high-resolution XRD/TEM)
Dislocation slip morphology (observed in situ via TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if there is no clear correlation between the measured magnitude of local lattice distortions and the observed differences in mechanical properties and dislocation behavior between the quinary baseline and the quaternary/ternary subsets, or if alloys with reduced compositional complexity exhibit the same or increased resistance to dislocation motion as indicated by similar or higher yield strengths.

System: Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8 (nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25) BCC refractory high-entropy alloy. Processing: Arc melting under argon atmosphere from 99.99 wt% purity elements, melted 10 times, drop-cast into 4-mm diameter rods, homogenized at 1200°C for 3 days, followed by water cooling.
